stem: A client with advanced chronic kidney disease has marked hyperphosphatemia. Which additional laboratory abnormality commonly accompanies this mineral-bone disturbance?
rationale: NCBI/StatPearls explains that declining kidney function impairs phosphate excretion and decreases active vitamin D production, contributing to hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia in CKD-mineral bone disorder. Therefore B is correct. Hypercalcemia is the opposite calcium pattern, while hypernatremia and hypermagnesemia are not the characteristic paired abnormality tested here.
educational_objective: Recognize the common hyperphosphatemia–hypocalcemia pattern of CKD-mineral bone disorder.
source_locator: Etiology/Pathophysiology — impaired phosphate excretion and decreased active vitamin D lead to hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia; secondary hyperparathyroidism may follow.
source_claim_supported: Advanced CKD with phosphate retention commonly produces hypocalcemia as part of CKD-MBD.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

source_original.stem: A client with advanced chronic kidney disease has marked hyperphosphatemia. Which additional laboratory abnormality commonly accompanies this mineral-bone disturbance?
source_original.rationale: In advanced CKD, impaired phosphate excretion and reduced calcitriol activity contribute to phosphate retention and lower serum calcium, often with secondary hyperparathyroidism. Hypocalcemia is therefore the best answer. Hypercalcemia is the opposite calcium pattern, while hypernatremia and hypermagnesemia are not the characteristic paired abnormality tested in CKD mineral-bone disorder.
source_original.source_detail: StatPearls Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder — Pathophysiology: declining kidney function impairs phosphate excretion and calcitriol production, contributing to hyperphosphatemia, lower serum calcium or hypocalcemia, and secondary hyperparathyroidism in advanced CKD. Current StatPearls CKD-Mineral Bone Disorder entry in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15. audit_findings.claim_audit: Uses common CKD-MBD relationship without claiming every CKD patient is hypocalcemic.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B matches the described CKD-MBD mechanism.
